mechanism: GLP-1 gut slowdown / delayed stomach emptying
ums_status: General motility-support criterion introduced before product; proprietary Motilli physiological mechanism not substantiated

segments.copy: If your stomach looks like this on a GLP-1, mine does too. I'm eating smaller meals, but I still get that tight, bloated feeling.
segments.visual: H01: Clothed side profile of the same fictional woman; she turns toward her phone camera, hand rests lightly on waistband.

segments.copy: Some days, a few bites of lunch leave me feeling so full I want to undo my jeans. I couldn't understand why eating less wasn't making that feeling go away.
segments.visual: H02: Overhead modest lunch plate; fork set down. At “undo my jeans”, cut to a distinct seated waistband detail.
segments.purpose: Give the explanation one specific experience to resolve.

segments.copy: Then I learned about GLP-1 gut slowdown. Medicines like Wegovy can slow how quickly the stomach empties, which means food can stay there longer after a meal.
segments.visual: S01: Authentic official medication information on tablet, highlight stomach emptying; short editor label GLP-1 gut slowdown.
segments.purpose: Supply the central new explanation early.

segments.copy: Normally, the muscles in my stomach mix the food and gradually move it into my small intestine. When that process slows down, the full feeling can last longer too.
segments.visual: S02: One isolated stomach-to-duodenum model shows mixing and gradual passage, with restrained timing schematic at “slows down”. No complete blockage or product.
segments.purpose: Explain the cause and immediate consequence once, in ordinary language.

segments.beat: Connect it back to her meal
segments.copy: That could help explain why even a small meal was leaving me uncomfortable. I'd been thinking about how much I ate, without thinking about how quickly my stomach was emptying.
segments.visual: H03: Three-quarter kitchen shot, woman looks from meal notes toward camera; no repeated lunch insert.
segments.purpose: Land amount-versus-movement as the one belief shift.

segments.copy: One night, I was scrolling through a Facebook GLP-1 support group when I noticed a gastroenterologist's comment under a post about bloating.
segments.visual: F01: Over-shoulder view of woman scrolling an illustrative support-group feed. Persistent prominent Dramatized example—not a real post. No real group name, personal profile, identity, likes or fabricated verification.
segments.purpose: Deliver the user-requested quick discovery context before the solution mechanism.

segments.copy: He wrote, 'If slow stomach emptying is the problem, you need to ask about supporting stomach motility—the movement that carries food into the intestine.'
segments.visual: F02: Readable illustrative comment card with the exact conditional wording; role label Fictional gastroenterologist. Same prominent Dramatized example—not a real post disclosure. No Motilli branding or product recommendation.
segments.purpose: Introduce stomach movement as the relevant solution target. This is invented dramatic dialogue, not a sourced clinician quotation or endorsement.

segments.beat: Name the solution criterion before the brand
segments.copy: That was what I'd been missing: a solution aimed at the movement itself. I started looking into motility support.
segments.visual: F03: Return to woman at kitchen table, phone lowered; editor label Motility = movement. Fresh narrator delivery, no replayed stomach anatomy or product footage.
segments.purpose: Make the mechanism she is investigating explicit before any Motilli mention. Motility support is a category, not proof of product uniqueness or efficacy.

segments.copy: While looking into that, I came across Motilli. It combines celery juice powder, prebiotic fiber, and chlorophyll in a daily gummy—a formula I could review with my prescriber.
segments.visual: PR01: First verified Motilli product-page reveal, then distinct actual bottle with ingredient labels. Hard internal cut at It combines. Remove fictional doctor and group UI before brand appears.
segments.purpose: Introduce Motilli as a product for evaluation after the desired mechanism has been explained; no doctor-product endorsement or demonstrated prokinetic effect.

segments.copy: And the routine is simple: two gummies before bed with a full glass of water. I liked being able to chew something instead of adding another capsule to my evening.
segments.visual: PR03: Close-up current directions, then distinct neutral gummy demonstration beside water; narrator does not consume product.
segments.purpose: Make the format and directions concrete without claiming better absorption.

segments.copy: What I want is simple too: finish a meal and get on with my evening, without spending the next few hours focused on how tight my stomach feels.
segments.visual: H04: Fictional woman talks from sofa in same home, hopeful but still describing a goal. No recovery montage or flat-belly transformation.
segments.purpose: Use one short aspiration that closes the opening loop.

segments.copy: Motilli has a ninety-day money-back guarantee from delivery, including opened bottles. That matters to me, because I'd want to judge my own experience before deciding whether to keep it in my routine.
segments.visual: PR04: Current bottle and clear guarantee text: 90 days from delivery; Opened bottles included; Terms apply.
segments.purpose: Use the verified offer without invented scarcity or results.

segments.visual: PR05: Stable current packshot, See Motilli CTA, guarantee reference; retain through end hold.
